The goal is: don't trust anyone. The solution is to use server relays over which you have maximum control, and to use more than one. Compartmentalize, so the underlings don't know who they serve or what they do!

Let's say you rent two $5/month virtual private servers, one in the Netherlands and one in Russia. They can be tiny basement businesses, among many thousands. They don't know anything about you as a person, only that you send them crypto-coin every X days for their services. (Means of avoiding traceability with digital currency transactions are explained elsewhere.) At a moment notice can add / switch to a virtual server relay in Iceland, Switzerland, Malaysia, Jordan, Brazil, etc.

  • From the perspective of the last relay server, they know the destination IPs of your traffic (which must also have application-level encryption like SSL or SSH).
